observations: PHP Arrays had two optional clarity issues: unexplained arrow-function reading and unlabeled output states.
PHP Control Flow had one clarity issue, but it was primarily a precision/type-boundary problem.
All three short JavaScript final reviews passed with no style issues; their repeated interaction wording is metadata, not evidence of learner-facing prose harm.
No reading-time, comprehension or human naturalness ratings were recorded.

gaps.qualityGapDefinition: A defect or missing control in one material or pipeline run, such as missing evidence, an overbroad claim, absent runtime verification or unclear exercise framing.
gaps.knowledgeGapDefinition: A missing prerequisite or topic in the whole knowledge map; it cannot be inferred from one article defect.
knowledgeGapInputObservations: The existence of PHP/JavaScript arrays and control-flow articles does not prove complete beginner paths.
Only PHP samples are published; publication coverage is not equivalent to knowledge-map completeness.
No Knowledge Gap analysis was run, so no missing topic is asserted.

architecturePrinciple.recommendation: Do not accelerate by adding agents. Reuse contracts, add deterministic read-only validators, remove repeated manual integrity work and escalate only evidence-backed exceptions to humans.
evidence: All five runs used the same four roles.
Two successful corrections were small hash-bound prose edits followed by full re-review, not Writer loops.
Most repeated work was deterministic validation, while claim scope and publication decisions required judgment.

recommendedNextExperiment.name: read-only verify:article contract spike
recommendedNextExperiment.scope: Specify fixtures and expected PASS/FAIL/NOT_APPLICABLE results for the five frozen samples before implementing any CLI.
recommendedNextExperiment.why: Highest repeated evidence, bounded risk and no need for a new agent or content mutation.

limitations: The two PHP samples are much larger and used richer research/runtime matrices than the three deliberately small B3 samples; counts are descriptive, not a benchmark.
PHP Arrays predates interaction metadata, so its interaction count is unknown rather than zero.
Recorded model labels are not reliable exact provider/model identifiers.
No elapsed-time, token, quota, monetary-cost or learner-outcome series exists.
